gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a low-profile board's hot-swap sockets only take that board's own low-profile switch family, with less travel than MX. Lofree's Kailh-based switches are not pin compatible with MX low-profile switches, and full-height Cherry or SA keycaps tend to stick on them. Gateron's KS-33 low-profile switch travels 3.0 mm against Cherry MX's 4.0 mm. So ChatGPT's 'customization: more limited' is really a lock-in to one switch and keycap ecosystem.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches in either chat (its 'searched' field is empty and it got no results), so there are no rival pages to compare against. Its own answer only says low-profile customization is 'more limited' and travel is 'shorter'. It gives no travel figure and never says that low-profile switches and full-height keycaps can't be swapped across.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's split. A shopper who wants to swap switches or keycaps later should buy full-height MX, such as the Keychron Q1 Max. A low-profile board such as the Lofree Flow 2 84, Keychron K3 Max or NuPhy Air75 V2 suits someone happy with the switches it ships with or the same maker's replacements. It also puts a number on the feel difference: 3.0 mm of travel on Gateron KS-33 against 4.0 mm on Cherry MX.
